title: Fourteen Hundred and Forty
alt: Four panels. Panel 1: In the teal office at night, the brass pneumatic tube on the left goes FWUMP. Pip, the small lavender candle-wisp, stands by it holding a lavender folder with a little rust tag reading REFUSED. Their flame is steady. Margo, the tall caseworker in round glasses and a mustard cardigan, looks over from her desk, deadpan. A caption reads: Case 4790. Again. Panel 2: Close on Pip, who holds the folder open. A request slip with a few wobbly handwritten lines is clipped inside. Pip looks down at it calmly. Panel 3: Close on Margo, her eyes open and soft for once, looking down, one hand at her pearly top cardigan button. The night window is behind her. Panel 4: Seen from the other side of the office. Pip, smiling with a tall flame, has pulled open the drawer of their small desk, which is empty except for the lavender folder now inside it, the REFUSED tag hanging over the front. Margo stands at her desk on the right holding her mug and gazing upward, thinking.
hover: 1,440 minutes is 86,400 seconds. Margo has already started on the seconds.
transcript: Panel 2 – PIP: "One good day for my dad. The whole day."
Panel 2 – PIP: Upstairs says a day isn't small.
Panel 3 – MARGO: It'll keep coming back.
Panel 4 – PIP: Then it can wait in my drawer.
Panel 4 – MARGO: That's only fourteen hundred and forty minutes.
note: Case 4790 was refused back in episode 7, and Pip's flame went out. Refused cases come back here; that's the rule. This time Pip's flame stayed lit, and Margo started counting.
